aciklama: NOTYA araclar-denetim, Canada (ca): the decisions of docs/araclar-denetim/CA.md as data. Research only: no code, pack, test or kit file was changed. Every source was read on 2026-10-10. State of a tool: done (switched on in this country), slot (placeholder, switched off), absent (in the shared kit, not in this country). Class: base (every role) or specialty-only (the roles listed). Verdict words for tools: keep, revise, remove, unverified (no Canadian source could be read: needs a local clinician); for a slot, keep means it stays switched off. For specialties: keep, rename, remove, add. A key ending in * is a proposed key that does not exist yet.
language: en-CA (English only; French and Quebec out of scope)

tools.change: Two items are plain tick-boxes: "Pre-operative laboratory tests done" and "Pre-operative imaging and its report seen", and the tool counts how many of five are done. The Canadian Anesthesiologists' Society's Choosing Wisely Canada list tells doctors not to order baseline laboratory tests, an ECG or a chest X-ray for patients without symptoms before low-risk surgery. A list that reads "incomplete" until tests are ticked pushes the other way. Change: word both items "where indicated" and let "not needed" count as done. Separately, the item "Consent ... obtained from a parent or guardian" assumes a rule most provinces do not have (earlier audit, A22): for a lawyer.

tools.change: The arithmetic is the published index as the code cites it (four regions, weights 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.4, total 0 to 72); the primary paper was not opened. The problem is the grade: the tool calls a score below 10 mild, 10 to 19.9 moderate and 20 or more severe. No Canadian source for those two cut-offs was found. The one Canadian paper read (a survey of Canadian dermatologists) says moderate and severe psoriasis have no agreed limits and cites the "rule of tens", under which a PASI above 10 already counts as severe. A score of 12 is therefore "Moderate" on this screen and "severe" by the rule that paper cites. Change: show the number without a grade, or take the grade from a Canadian dermatologist with its source.
tools.licence: Published index; no licence page was read: unclear.

tools.change: Weight is taken in kilograms only, which is what ISMP Canada asks for. Two points, both in the kit and so in every country. (1) ROUNDING TO CHECK: the volume for one dose is rounded to the nearest 0.1 mL and only the rounded figure is shown, with a warning only below 0.1 mL. Between 0.1 and 1 mL that rounding moves the volume by several per cent, and near 0.15 mL by about a third, while the milligram figure beside it stays exact. A pharmacist or pediatrician should say how small volumes are to be shown. (2) Visibility: this report's judgement, not from a source, is that family physicians and emergency physicians need the same arithmetic for the children they see (Part 3).

tools.change: LICENCE PROBLEM, AND IT IS SWITCHED ON. The tool offers and prints the categories "BI-RADS 0" to "BI-RADS 6". Clinically that is right for Canada: the Canadian Association of Radiologists' 2026 breast guideline works in BI-RADS categories. But BI-RADS is a registered trademark of the American College of Radiology, and the College says a vendor must "enter into a copyright licensing agreement" to put BI-RADS into commercial software. No such agreement is recorded. Change: until the owner has the licence, show the outline without the BI-RADS name and categories (a general report outline), or switch the tool off.
tools.licence: NEEDS A LICENCE from the American College of Radiology for commercial software; BI-RADS is its registered trademark.

One boundary differs from the secondary source read: that source puts a score of exactly 3.2 in low activity (low runs up to 3.2, moderate starts above it), while the kit puts 3.2 in moderate and the screen says "Low activity (2.6 to 3.19)". The score is shown to two decimals, so 3.20 can occur. Change in the kit (every country): 3.2 belongs to low. tools.change: Two points. (1) Unit label: this pack shows the value in µg/L, marked unverified. The Canadian Urological Association's 2022 guideline that was read writes PSA in ng/mL. The two are the same number, but a urologist should see the unit their guideline and their laboratory print: show "µg/L (= ng/mL)" or confirm per province. (2) Use: no Canadian source that was read recommends PSA velocity. The Association's guideline that could be opened does not use the term, its screening guideline could not be opened, and the Canadian Task Force recommends against PSA screening at every age. The tool shows no threshold, which is right; a Canadian urologist should say whether it is wanted at all.

tools.change: SAFETY: THE STAGES ARE NOT CANADA'S. The tool records stage 0 to 5 with its own names. The Canadian Guideline on Concussion in Sport (Parachute, 2nd edition, 2024) has six steps numbered 1 to 6, with step 2 split into 2A and 2B, different names, and medical clearance required before step 4. "Stage 4" written from this tool means contact training; step 4 of the Canadian guideline is non-contact training drills. A note carried to a coach, a school or another doctor would be read one step out, on an athlete with a head injury. Change (needs a kit change: the options are fixed at 0 to 5): replace by the Canadian steps, with the return-to-school steps beside them (proposed tool in Part 2). Until then, switch off for Canada.
tools.licence: The Canadian guideline is © Parachute, 2024; no terms for reuse are stated in it: ask Parachute.

tools.change: A log with one calculation: this week's training minutes divided by the earlier weekly average, flagged from 1.3 and from 1.5 after a 2016 paper. No Canadian source was read that recommends this ratio or these two limits. Needs a Canadian sport and exercise medicine physician.

tools.change: Rightly off today: the kit sorts albuminuria in mg/g after converting, and Canada's laboratories and guidelines work in mg/mmol with their own round limits (the British Columbia guideline: below 3.0, 3.0 to 30.0, above 30.0 mg/mmol). The GFR categories were not re-read from a source (the guideline's figure is an image). Family medicine should see the finished tool too.

addTools.proposedName: Unit converter: pounds, feet and inches, Fahrenheit to kilograms, centimetres, Celsius
addTools.nationalSource: ISMP Canada (medication-safety body supported by Health Canada) tells patients and parents to know and record weight in kilograms, and to have a weight in pounds converted.
addTools.formulaCitation: The exact defined factors, already in the kit (lib/ulke/araclar/birimler.ts): 1 in = 2.54 cm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg.
addTools.note: ISMP Canada's advice exists because patients and home scales still use pounds while doses are worked out in kilograms. The earlier audit found that the product offers no second unit anywhere.

addTools.proposedName: Estimated GFR (CKD-EPI 2021, creatinine in µmol/L), adults
addTools.nationalSource: Alberta Precision Laboratories moved to the 2021 CKD-EPI equation on 2026-01-20 for patients aged 18 and older and states that it is supported by the Canadian Society of Nephrology; a 2022 CMAJ article calls for the race-free equations across Canada (Ontario had already acted).
addTools.formulaCitation: Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, et al. New creatinine- and cystatin C-based equations to estimate GFR without race. N Engl J Med 2021;385(19):1737-1749.
addTools.licence: free to implement (a published equation); not confirmed with the publisher
addTools.note: Adults only: the kit has no way to hold a tool back by the patient's age. Which equation each province's laboratories report was verified for Alberta only.

addTools.proposedName: Blood pressure: average of the readings and Hypertension Canada's category, adults
addTools.nationalSource: Hypertension Canada, guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of hypertension in adults in primary care (CMAJ, 2025): three readings one minute apart with a validated automated device, averaged; the diagnostic threshold and the single treatment target are in its Table 2 and Figures 2 and 3.
addTools.formulaCitation: Goupil R, Tsuyuki RT, Santesso N, et al. Hypertension Canada guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of hypertension in adults in primary care. CMAJ 2025 (26 May); doi:10.1503/cmaj.241770.
addTools.licence: free to implement the numbers; the guideline's figures are the publisher's
addTools.note: Adults only. The threshold was lowered in 2025 from the 2020 guideline, so a tool carried over with older numbers would be wrong.

addTools.nationalSource: CTAS National Advisory Committee (National Emergency Nurses Association with the Canadian Association of Emergency Physicians).
addTools.formulaCitation: Bullard MJ, Musgrave E, Warren D, et al. Revisions to the Canadian Emergency Department Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) guidelines 2016. CJEM 2017;19(S2):S18-S27. Paediatric: Warren DW, et al. CJEM 2008;10(3):224-232.
addTools.licence: NEEDS PERMISSION: licensing is handled by the Canadian Association of Emergency Physicians (contact on the CTAS licensing page); the terms for software are not published.
addTools.note: Replaces the ESI slot. Like the ESI record it would only record the level the triage nurse or doctor chose; it must not work the level out. The CTAS courses are run through the emergency nurses' association: whether an emergency physician wants this in a doctor's tool at all is for a local emergency physician.

addTools.proposedName: Ten-year cardiovascular risk (Framingham Risk Score), in mmol/L
addTools.nationalSource: British Columbia guideline on primary prevention (2021) recommends the Framingham Risk Score and follows the Canadian Cardiovascular Society's 2021 lipid guideline, whose resources include a Framingham calculator; Hypertension Canada 2025 uses the same score as a high-risk criterion.
addTools.formulaCitation: D'Agostino RB Sr, Vasan RS, Pencina MJ, et al. General cardiovascular risk profile for use in primary care: the Framingham Heart Study. Circulation 2008;117(6):743-753. Canadian guideline: Pearson GJ, Thanassoulis G, Anderson TJ, et al. Can J Cardiol 2021;37(8):1129-1150.
addTools.licence: free to implement from the primary paper; unclear for the Society's own charts (ask the Canadian Cardiovascular Society)
addTools.note: Fills the slot cardiovascular-risk. The guideline's own text could not be opened (its chapters and the PubMed record were not readable), so any Canadian adjustment to the score must be taken from the guideline by a clinician.

addTools.proposedName: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation: the CCS algorithm (CHADS-65)
addTools.nationalSource: Canadian Cardiovascular Society / Canadian Heart Rhythm Society 2020 guideline, recommendation 17 and Figure 8; Thrombosis Canada's guide (2024) rests on the same algorithm.
addTools.formulaCitation: Andrade JG, Aguilar M, Atzema C, et al. The 2020 Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Heart Rhythm Society comprehensive guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation. Can J Cardiol 2020;36(12):1847-1948.
addTools.licence: unclear: the algorithm is the Society's figure. The logic can be implemented; ask the Canadian Cardiovascular Society before copying the figure or its wording.
addTools.note: A Canadian rule that the other English-speaking countries do not use: it must exist in the Canada pack only. It names a class of medicine, not a medicine or a dose.

addTools.proposedName: Kidney Failure Risk Equation (2 and 5 years), with albumin-to-creatinine ratio in mg/mmol
addTools.nationalSource: Ontario's KidneyWise toolkit made a 5-year risk by this equation a referral criterion (2023 update). British Columbia's guideline describes it but says its role "has yet to be established in routine clinical practice".
addTools.formulaCitation: Tangri N, Stevens LA, Griffith J, et al. A predictive model for progression of chronic kidney disease to kidney failure. JAMA 2011;305(15):1553-1559. Tangri N, Grams ME, Levey AS, et al. JAMA 2016;315(2):164-174.
addTools.licence: unclear: a published equation of Canadian origin; its owners' terms were not read
addTools.note: PROVINCIAL DIFFERENCE, noted and not resolved: a referral criterion in Ontario, not established in British Columbia. The tool should give the risk and leave the referral rule to the province.

addTools.nationalSource: Diabetes Canada points health-care providers to CANRISK for deciding who to screen; the Canadian Task Force (2012) accepts CANRISK as an alternative to the calculator it prefers.
addTools.formulaCitation: Robinson CA, Agarwal G, Nerenberg K. Validating the CANRISK prognostic model for assessing diabetes risk in Canada's multi-ethnic population. Chronic Dis Inj Can 2011;32(1):19-31.
addTools.licence: NEEDS PERMISSION / unclear: the questionnaire is the federal government's (hosted on a Government of Canada site); the terms for putting its wording in a commercial product were not read.
addTools.note: A questionnaire: its wording may not be reproduced until the federal owner agrees.

addTools.proposedName: Fracture risk: link to FRAX for Canada, and CAROC
addTools.nationalSource: Osteoporosis Canada's 2023 guideline calls FRAX (the Canadian version) "the preferred tool for fracture risk estimation" and names CAROC as a validated alternative; the Canadian Task Force (2023) starts from the Canadian FRAX without bone density.
addTools.formulaCitation: FRAX: Kanis JA, Johnell O, Oden A, Johansson H, McCloskey E. Osteoporos Int 2008;19:385-397. CAROC: Leslie WD, Berger C, Langsetmo L, et al. Osteoporos Int 2011;22(6):1873-1883.
addTools.licence: FRAX: the calculation is not published in full and is run on the University of Sheffield's site (Osteoporosis Canada links there): link out only; a licence would be needed to embed it (terms not read). CAROC: unclear.
addTools.note: A link-out tile with the inputs to have ready, not a calculator. The Task Force recommends against screening men and women under 65.

addTools.proposedName: Growth: WHO Growth Charts for Canada (percentiles and plots, birth to 19 years)
addTools.nationalSource: Dietitians of Canada with the Canadian Paediatric Society, the College of Family Physicians of Canada and Community Health Nurses of Canada (2014 redesign, reviewed 2019); recommended by the Canadian Pediatric Endocrine Group; used by the Rourke Baby Record.
addTools.formulaCitation: WHO Multicentre Growth Reference Study Group. WHO Child Growth Standards. Acta Paediatr Suppl 2006;450:76-85. de Onis M, et al. Development of a WHO growth reference for school-aged children and adolescents. Bull World Health Organ 2007;85:660-667. Canadian use: A health professional's guide for using the WHO growth charts for Canada (2014).
addTools.licence: NEEDS PERMISSION: the Canadian charts and guide are © Dietitians of Canada and Canadian Paediatric Society, "For non-commercial use only". The WHO tables underneath: WHO's terms not read.
addTools.note: Fills the slot growth-percentiles. Canada offers two chart sets with different percentile lines; a clinician chooses. Premature infants are plotted at corrected age.

addTools.proposedName: Rourke Baby Record: well-baby and well-child visit record (birth to 5 years)
addTools.nationalSource: Endorsed by the Canadian Paediatric Society, the College of Family Physicians of Canada and Dietitians of Canada.
addTools.licence: NEEDS A LICENCE AGREEMENT, offered free of charge to record-system companies on condition that the latest edition is used (contact named in its FAQ).
addTools.note: Replaces the idea of a development-screening panel. It is a whole visit record (its download addresses show a national and an Ontario edition), so it is a large piece of licensed content, not a calculator.

addTools.proposedName: Concussion: Canadian return-to-sport and return-to-school steps
addTools.nationalSource: Parachute, Canadian Guideline on Concussion in Sport, 2nd edition (2024), funded by the Public Health Agency of Canada.
addTools.formulaCitation: Parachute. Canadian Guideline on Concussion in Sport, 2nd edition. Toronto: Parachute; 2024. International basis: Patricios JS, Schneider KJ, Dvorak J, et al. Consensus statement on concussion in sport: the 6th International Conference on Concussion in Sport, Amsterdam, October 2022. Br J Sports Med 2023;57:695-711.
addTools.licence: unclear: © Parachute, 2024, with no reuse terms in the document: ask Parachute.
addTools.note: Replaces rtp-basamak in Canada. Records the step the doctor chose and whether medical clearance was given; proposes no timing.

addTools.proposedName: Ottawa Ankle Rules, Ottawa Knee Rule, Canadian C-Spine Rule, Canadian CT Head Rule
addTools.nationalSource: Developed at the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute (Dr. Ian Stiell); described by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research.
addTools.formulaCitation: Ankle: Stiell IG, Greenberg GH, McKnight RD, et al. Ann Emerg Med 1992;21(4):384-390. Knee: Stiell IG, Greenberg GH, Wells GA, et al. Ann Emerg Med 1995;26(4):405-413. C-spine: Stiell IG, Wells GA, Vandemheen KL, et al. JAMA 2001;286(15):1841-1848. CT head: Stiell IG, Wells GA, Vandemheen K, et al. Lancet 2001;357(9266):1391-1396.
addTools.licence: unclear: the Institute's page carries "all rights reserved" and no free-use statement: ask the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute.
addTools.note: Four separate checklists. Each has age limits and exclusions that must be taken from the primary paper by a clinician.

addTools.proposedName: Stroke severity record: NIHSS and the Canadian Neurological Scale
addTools.nationalSource: Canadian Stroke Best Practice Recommendations, 7th edition (Heart and Stroke Foundation of Canada): NIHSS for the first assessment; both scales listed in Appendix 3 as free downloads.
addTools.formulaCitation: NIHSS: Brott T, Adams HP Jr, Olinger CP, et al. Stroke 1989;20(7):864-870. Canadian Neurological Scale: Côté R, Hachinski VC, Shurvell BL, Norris JW, Wolfson C. Stroke 1986;17(4):731-737.
addTools.licence: unclear: listed as free to download; terms for showing the item wording in a commercial product were not read. Until then the doctor types the total and the tool records it.

addTools.proposedName: Pregnancy dating by first-trimester ultrasound (SOGC Guideline No. 388)
addTools.nationalSource: Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada, Guideline No. 388, as applied in Nova Scotia's provincial guideline (2023).
addTools.formulaCitation: Butt K, Lim KI. Guideline No. 388: Determination of gestational age by ultrasound. J Obstet Gynaecol Can 2019;41(10):1497-1507.
addTools.licence: unclear: the Society's reuse terms were not read; the rule of which date wins must be taken from the guideline by a clinician.
addTools.note: Makes the slot pregnancy-calendar safe for Canada. The Society's own page could not be reached; the guideline was read only as a province quotes it.

kitGaps.gap: The five English-speaking countries must use exactly the same 40 role keys (countries/_dil/en/klinik/roller.ts; lib/ulke/rolEslemesi.test.ts fails otherwise). Canada can rename a role (rolAdlari) but cannot add, split or drop one alone.
kitGaps.blocks: Cardiac Surgery / Vascular Surgery split; the six specialties and two clinic professions to add.

kitGaps.gap: Which roles see a tool is written once in the shared English set (HamArac.roller). A country can only switch a tool off (araclar.kapali).
kitGaps.blocks: Showing dose arithmetic, PHQ-9, the kidney tool or the blood-pressure follow-up to family medicine in Canada only; showing audiometry to audiologists.

kitGaps.gap: A pack takes the shared English list minus what it closes; it has no list of tools of its own.
kitGaps.blocks: CTAS, the CCS algorithm (CHADS-65), the Canadian concussion steps, the Kidney Failure Risk Equation, CANRISK: tools that must exist in Canada and in no other English-speaking country.

kitGaps.gap: A country may re-word a tool's fields, numbers, bands and warnings (degisen) but not its name, its options or the line under the result, and cannot change how many options or bands the kit has.
kitGaps.blocks: Seven hearing grades instead of six; six concussion steps numbered 1 to 6 with 2A and 2B instead of stages 0 to 5; removing the BI-RADS names from the report outline.

kitGaps.gap: The kit knows a country and nothing smaller. Canada's content is provincial.
kitGaps.blocks: Vaccination schedules, notifiable diseases, kidney referral criteria, laboratory units and report formats, consent of minors, billing codes, crisis lines.

kitGaps.gap: A tool cannot be held back, or switch its arithmetic, by the patient's age.
kitGaps.blocks: Adult-only eGFR and blood pressure; EASI for a child under 8.

kitGaps.gap: A laboratory value is converted to the kit's unit and classified there; a country cannot state category limits in its own unit.
kitGaps.blocks: The two KDIGO tools in mg/mmol.

kitGaps.gap: A tool is either base (all 40 roles, allied professions included) or lists its roles. There is no class "every doctor".
kitGaps.blocks: Prescription, interactions, requests, coding, eGFR and blood pressure for the 35 doctor roles without showing them to a physiotherapist or an audiologist (possible today only by spelling out 35 keys per tool).

kitGaps.gap: Tool kinds are formula, scale, list, dates and kit screen. There is no tile that opens an outside calculator with the inputs listed.
kitGaps.blocks: FRAX for Canada, which may not be reimplemented.
